gitea/gitea.reason: 28.3.0 is the newest Gitea release. Both findings are the Alpine 3.24 base's libexpat, fixed in 2.10.0-r0 and taken when Gitea rebuilds its image. It is there for the base's git, whose http-push (WebDAV) is the one part that parses XML with it, and Gitea never runs it: Gitea is a Go binary, serves Git over its own smart HTTP and SSH, and reads XML with Go's encoding/xml.

grafana/grafana.reason: 13.3.0 is the newest Grafana release. The Tempo findings are in the Tempo plugin, which grafana.ini disables, so Grafana never starts it. The Go findings (stdlib 1.26.7 and golang.org/x/net, compiled into every bundled datasource plugin) each need a hostile HTTP/2 or TLS peer, or a crafted request to a Go file server. A plugin serves only Grafana, over its local go-plugin connection, and the two grafana.ini leaves enabled (PostgreSQL and Loki) speak only to this stack's own databases and Loki.

jryberg/mosquitto-exporter.reason: v0.7.9 is the release the chart pins. Its Go binary carries five Go findings (stdlib and golang.org/x/net); v0.8.0 is built with a newer Go, scans clean of them, and Renovate proposes it once its three-day wait passes, which retires those five. The rest are Debian 13 base packages (Perl, PCRE2, SQLite, gzip, OpenSSL) that v0.8.0 still carries and the container never runs: its one process is /mosquitto_exporter, a static binary.

node.reason: 24.22.2 is the newest Node 24 release; Node 26 is a major and moves on its own. npm is never run: the storage-init Job runs `node /app/storage-init.mjs`. All six are npm's own dependencies under /usr/local/lib/node_modules/npm; the fetch the script uses is the undici built into the node binary.

quay.io/prometheuscommunity/postgres-exp.reason: v0.20.1 is still the newest release (2026-07-08). The findings are Go stdlib and golang.org/x/crypto, net and text compiled into it. It runs as a sidecar in each database pod, reads only its own database over loopback and serves /metrics to the chart's Alloy, so no untrusted peer reaches it. A release built with a newer Go clears them.

supabase/gotrue.reason: v2.197.0 is upstream's pin (Supabase's compose of 2026-10-16). Alpine's OpenSSL is never loaded: auth is a Go binary, and the flaw is in OpenSSL's QUIC server. In the binary, gRPC-Go is there for the OTLP exporters, which the chart does not configure, and GoTrue runs no gRPC server. It serves plain HTTP/1.1 to the gateway and calls no HTTP service (its access-token hook is a database function), so it has no TLS listener for the ECH flaw, no HTTP/2 for the SETTINGS flaw, and it serves no files through net/http for the Range flaw. go-jose parses JWKs only from an external identity provider's issuer: the chart enables none and no custom provider exists, so an ID-token sign-in is refused before any is fetched. x509's denylist of distrusted public intermediates matters only to a chain through one of them: GoTrue's connection to the site's mail relay, which an attacker would have to sit on the path of.

supabase/postgres.reason: 17.6.1.175 stays: upstream's compose names the older 17.6.1.136, and a server never moves back. The chart runs this image only as the psql and pg_dump client, in Jobs and init containers that each set their own command, so the image's entrypoint and the gosu it starts (every Go finding) never run. Alpine's curl and libcurl, and the brotli only libcurl loads, are never run either: no container of this image runs curl, and its psql and pg_dump come from the image's Nix store with that store's own libraries.

supabase/postgres-meta.reason: v0.100.0 is upstream's pin (Supabase's compose of 2026-10-16). It is in-cluster only: neither a route nor the gateway reaches it, and its one client is Studio's server. It has no login of its own and runs whatever SQL a request sends as supabase_admin, so a pod that can reach it already holds the database, and none of these gives such a pod more. Within that, fastify's and fast-uri's flaws bypass checks that guard nothing here (fast-uri parses only its own schemas' ids); find-my-way's needs an HTTP/2 server and proxy-addr's a trusted proxy, and it has neither; piscina and tinypool are prototype-pollution gadgets with no pollution to use. npm's own packages and the Debian base's Perl and OpenSSL are never run: the container runs node dist/server/server.js, and the node binary links neither.

supabase/realtime.reason: v2.143.3 is upstream's pin (Supabase's compose of 2026-10-16). All are Debian 13.6 base packages. The container runs the Erlang release, whose crypto library links libcrypto alone, and the probes, which run the openssl tool to sign a token locally and curl for one plain-HTTP GET to localhost: so no QUIC or DTLS for OpenSSL, and no TLS, proxy, upload, HTTP/2, SSH or compressed body for curl, which leaves libssh2 and brotli idle. Python and pyasn1 (the AWS CLI's), jq, Perl, gzip, expat, PCRE2 and SQLite serve start-script branches the chart never takes (the crash-dump upload, the cluster certificates) or nothing at all. util-linux's are in mount and in libblkid's partition probe, and the container can neither mount nor see a block device: it runs as nobody with every capability dropped.

supabase/storage-api.reason: v1.81.0 is upstream's pin (Supabase's compose of 2026-10-16); v1.84.30, Renovate's proposal, still carries 26 of these, busboy's two among them. Alpine's Python, and the expat only Python loads, never run: the container runs node dist/start/server.js, and the node binary links neither. npm's own packages are never run either. fastify's four need a sibling plugin's private not-found handler, a dependencies header schema, a false schema or an async Ajv schema, and storage-api has none (its not-found handlers all answer the same 404). fast-uri parses only the $id and $ref of storage-api's own schemas, never a request's URL. undici, ip-address, gRPC-JS and the Jaeger propagator sit idle: image transformation and its rate limiter, webhooks, the CDN purge, cluster discovery, profiling and tracing are all off and no proxy is set, so storage-api opens no outbound HTTP, WebSocket or SOCKS connection and runs no gRPC server, and the OTel SDK registers the Jaeger propagator only when OTEL_PROPAGATORS names it. systeminformation's flaw is in a Windows-only PowerShell path, and brace-expansion is minimatch's, matching patterns from code. busboy's crafted part header (CVE-2026-19481) fails only its own request: fastify-multipart pipes the body into busboy and handles its errors. busboy's loop on a boundary of exactly 252 bytes (CVE-2026-19484) gets no such boundary from outside the cluster. The gateway refuses, above every route to storage-api, a multipart boundary over 70 characters, the most RFC 2046 allows (section 5.1.1), and a multipart Content-Type over 200 characters or outside printable ASCII, which keeps every other spelling busboy reads (spaces, quotes, boundary*=charset'') under 252 bytes. The chart also turns off the S3 protocol, whose routes read a form before any credential. Inside the cluster a pod could still send one straight to supabase-storage:5000, unless networkPolicy.enabled limits who reaches it.

supabase/studio.reason: 2026.10.12-sha-3699278 is upstream's pin (Supabase's compose of 2026-10-16). No signed-out request reaches it. The chart publishes no route to Studio unless ingress.routes.studio is on, and that route ends at the gateway's studio listener, whose one route sends a request without a session to the sign-in and refuses every role but Administrator before Studio sees it; inside the cluster, supabase-studio:3000 is already the database owner's console with no login. The Debian base's kernel headers are not code, and its OpenSSL, expat and brotli serve git, Python and the openssl tool, which the server never runs; the node binary links none of them. npm's and pnpm's own packages are never run: the container runs node apps/studio/server.js. In the server, Next.js answers /_next/image with 404 because the self-hosted build sets images.unoptimized (and leaves sharp out), and the build has no Server Actions and no use cache; Sentry's tunnel route is set only in Supabase's hosted build; simple-git is braintrust's, run with fixed arguments to read a repository's metadata, and /app is not a repository; DOMPurify is never called with SAFE_FOR_TEMPLATES, a DOM-returning mode or IN_PLACE; markdown-it renders GraphiQL's schema descriptions, which only the database owner writes; and the MCP server at /api/mcp answers only an Administrator through that door, who already runs SQL as the owner there.
